setting: Blackwood Manor, during a storm-bound dinner party

locations.name: The Study
locations.description: Where Eleanor was found. Heavy oak door, one window latched from inside.

locations.name: The Dining Room
locations.description: Where the party gathered for dinner and after-dinner drinks.

locations.name: The Garden Path
locations.description: A gravel path along the east wing, exposed to the storm.

events.description: Dinner is served to the full party.
Raised voices are heard coming from the study.
Eleanor's body is discovered in the study.

suspects.name: James Calloway
suspects.alibi_claim: I was in the dining room with everyone the entire evening after dinner.
suspects.secret: He had been quietly embezzling from the partnership for over a year.

knowledge.fact: I did step outside briefly around nine, just to get some air.
Eleanor and I had some disagreements about the business finances, but nothing serious.

suspects.name: Priya Voss
suspects.alibi_claim: I was walking alone on the garden path, reading a letter I'd received.
suspects.secret: The letter was from an ex-fiancé; she was embarrassed, not involved in the death.

knowledge.fact: I was upset about a personal letter, that's why I went out to the garden alone.
I heard raised voices coming from the study, around a quarter to nine.

suspects.name: Mr. Hendricks
suspects.alibi_claim: I was outside at the woodshed, collecting firewood for the evening.

knowledge.fact: I went out to the shed for firewood around half past eight.
Mr. Calloway asked me not to disturb him and Mrs. Voss while they spoke privately in the study.

evidence.description: A financial ledger showing a discrepancy of several thousand pounds, unexplained.
A brandy glass with two distinct sets of fingerprints, found near the desk.
Eleanor's pocket watch, stopped at 9:12 PM.
A short note in the butler's hand, recording that he was asked to keep everyone away from the study after 8:45.
A torn, tear-stained letter addressed to Priya, signed by someone other than the victim.
A pair of muddy shoes left by the garden door, matching the storm-soaked path outside.

solution.motive_text: Concealing embezzlement from the business partnership.
solution.method_text: Confronted Eleanor over the ledger and struck her during their argument in the study.

metadata.note: Places him at the scene near the time of death.
Contradicts his claim of never leaving the dining room.
Time of death aligns with his unaccounted-for window.
Explains why she was genuinely in the garden — unrelated to the case.
Consistent with his firewood errand — unrelated to the case.
